newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's Pliva may consider new share issue later.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's Pliva may consider new share issue later.

text.p: Pharmaceutical company Pliva d.d., the first firm in Croatia to list its shares abroad, said on Monday it might consider a new issue at a later stage to finance further development.
"Our investment cycle at the moment does not require a new issue of shares, but it may be necessary for some future project," chief executive Zeljko Covic told a news conference.
He said the company's total investment by year 2000 could reach some 400 million German marks. It is currently working on six different projects in various stages of development.
Pliva spent 63 million kuna for long-term investments between January and June of 1996, compared to 46.4 million a year ago, Covic said.
Its first-half pre-tax profit jumped over 56 percent to 368.3 million kuna thanks to a 15.1 percent rise in sales, stronger exports and efficient cost cutting measures.
Preliminary net profit was estimated at 283.9 million kuna, up 27.6 percent from the first six months of 1995. Per share earnings rose to 520 from 457 kuna.

The company was privatised through an international share offering earlier this year. Private investors, including the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) now control some 58 percent of its stock. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
